summary: Join our specialized course on GIS and Remote Sensing, designed for agriculture and food security professionals. Address climate change challenges effectively.
lede: GIS and remote sensing in agriculture, food security, and climate change combine spatial data analysis with satellite imagery to monitor crop health, manage resources, assess climate vulnerabilities, and support food availability planning. This course helps you turn raw geospatial data into actionable intelligence for agricultural decision-making. Through hands-on work with QGIS and Google Earth Engine, you will practice vegetation monitoring, Enhanced Vegetation Index calculation, soil moisture anomaly mapping, land suitability analysis, and food security vulnerability mapping. You will also explore land use classification, climate risk modeling, and machine learning for crop classification while learning to produce clear spatial reports despite limited field data, cloud cover, and rapid environmental change.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for professionals tasked with managing agricultural resources and ensuring food stability in a changing climate.
modules: Vegetation Indices and Crop Health Monitoring
Climate Change Impact and Risk Assessment
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of agricultural concepts and be comfortable using a computer for data entry. No prior GIS experience is required, though familiarity with Microsoft Excel is highly recommended. You will need a laptop with at least 8GB of RAM to run the required open-source software.
